explanation: Flood-fill white cells reachable from any boundary. Those cells are protected; every remaining white cell belongs to an enclosed region and becomes black.
timeComplexity: O(rows × columns) Every cell is marked once and generates at most four neighbor attempts.
spaceComplexity: O(rows × columns) The queue and, in C#/JavaScript, visited bitmap can hold O(rows×columns) entries.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: The BFS marks exactly the white cells connected by white steps to a boundary: boundary white cells initialize it and each expansion follows an allowed adjacency. Thus unmarked white cells, and only those cells, are enclosed. Recoloring that complement preserves every boundary-connected region.
walkthrough: On ["BBBW","BWBW","BBBW"], the rightmost white column touches the boundary and remains white. The lone interior white cell is surrounded by black and becomes black, giving ["BBBW","BBBW","BBBW"].
edgeCases: White cells connected diagonally alone are not connected.
A boundary white component is never filled.
